verdict.rationale: Appwrite can be installed and run on any OS with a Docker CLI, which lets a developer run the full backend stack on a local machine. The CLI can target a self-hosted endpoint, functions are marketed as 'develop locally, deploy when ready', and a community user praises the containerized setup for offline development and testing. However, the docs frame this as self-hosting for production rather than a dedicated local emulator or local-dev workflow, and promoting a local setup to Cloud is only implied through migrations and the CLI's endpoint flag. missing for 10: dedicated emulator or local-dev CLI command (e.g. a local start command), first-party documentation of an end-to-end local-to-deploy workflow covering all services, hands-on corroboration beyond a single community comment.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole backend stack locally with an emulator or CLI before deploying

citations.quote: You can install and run Appwrite on any operating system that can run a Docker CLI.
13+ runtimes. Develop locally, deploy when ready.
Add the --endpoint flag if you're using a self-hosted instance of Appwrite.
You can also migrate between Appwrite Cloud and self-hosted.
They liked that Appwrite provides a containerized setup, which should make distributed development and testing easier.
